-- to “zero heat” is available. The common structural pattern is monotone transfer:
-- reductions transfer efficient solvability, while entropy loss transfers to work cost.
-- Critique (Critic): The extended Church–Turing thesis and P = NP remain explicit
-- hypotheses, not purported consequences. Jarzynski dynamics, positivity of k and T,
-- and a normalized finite probability distribution are essential boundaries. The model
-- does not claim that every decision procedure erases a bit; it applies only when the
-- proposed implementation realizes the specified erasure process.
-- Synthesis (Principal Investigator): The strongest surviving statement is a no-go
-- bridge: collapse yields efficient demons, but an efficient erasing demon still has
-- positive mean work, and therefore cannot be a zero-work second-law counterexample.
-- !-- end Lab Notes -- !--

/-- **Physical NP-hardness collapse.** If an NP-hard demon is physically realizable
within a polynomial resource bound, the extended Church–Turing thesis and closure
under reductions force every nondeterministic-polynomial problem into the
polynomial-time machine class. -/
theorem physical_npHard_demon_forces_collapse {α : Type*}
    (M : PhysicalComplexityModel α) (demon : Set α)
    (hhard : IsNPHardDemon M demon) (hphysical : demon ∈ M.physicalPoly) :
    PCollapsesNP M := by
  have heasy : demon ∈ M.polyTM := M.extendedChurchTuring hphysical
  exact completeness_transfer hhard M.polyClosedUnderReductions heasy

/-- Under the collapse hypothesis, every nondeterministic-polynomial demon problem
has a polynomial-time machine implementation. -/
theorem collapse_makes_demon_efficient {α : Type*}
    (M : PhysicalComplexityModel α) (demon : Set α)
    (hcollapse : PCollapsesNP M)
    (hdemon : demon ∈ M.nondeterministicPoly) :
    demon ∈ M.polyTM := by
  exact hcollapse hdemon

/-- **Complexity–thermodynamics separation.** Even when a P/NP collapse makes a demon
problem polynomial-time decidable, an implementation that erases a uniformly unknown
bit and obeys the finite Jarzynski equality at positive temperature has strictly
positive mean work. -/
theorem efficient_erasing_demon_has_positive_work
    {α Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω]
    (M : PhysicalComplexityModel α) (demon : Set α)
    (hcollapse : PCollapsesNP M)
    (hdemon : demon ∈ M.nondeterministicPoly)
    (p : Ω → ℝ) (hp : IsPMF p) (W : Ω → ℝ)
    (k T : ℝ) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hJ : JarzynskiCondition p W (k * T)⁻¹ (k * T * Real.log 2)) :
    demon ∈ M.polyTM ∧ ¬ Function.Injective erasure ∧ 0 < expect p W := by
  have hefficient := collapse_makes_demon_efficient M demon hcollapse hdemon
  rcases logical_to_thermodynamic_irreversibility p hp W k T hk hT hJ with
    ⟨hirreversible, hwork⟩
  exact ⟨hefficient, hirreversible, hwork⟩

/-- **No zero-work Maxwell demon from P = NP.** Under the same finite thermodynamic
assumptions, the conjunction “the demon is polynomial-time” and “its mean erasure
work is zero” is impossible.  The contradiction is quantitative: Landauer's lower
bound is strictly positive. -/
theorem no_zero_work_demon_from_collapse
    {α Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω]
    (M : PhysicalComplexityModel α) (demon : Set α)
    (hcollapse : PCollapsesNP M)
    (hdemon : demon ∈ M.nondeterministicPoly)
    (p : Ω → ℝ) (hp : IsPMF p) (W : Ω → ℝ)
    (k T : ℝ) (hk : 0 < k) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hJ : JarzynskiCondition p W (k * T)⁻¹ (k * T * Real.log 2)) :
    ¬ (demon ∈ M.polyTM ∧ expect p W = 0) := by
  intro hzero
  have hbridge := efficient_erasing_demon_has_positive_work
    M demon hcollapse hdemon p hp W k T hk hT hJ
  rcases hbridge with ⟨_, _, hpositive⟩
  linarith [hzero.2]

/-- The physical simulation thesis and an NP-hard polynomial physical process together
identify the deterministic and nondeterministic classes extensionally. -/
theorem physical_npHard_demon_yields_class_equality {α : Type*}
    (M : PhysicalComplexityModel α) (demon : Set α)
    (hhard : IsNPHardDemon M demon) (hphysical : demon ∈ M.physicalPoly) :
    M.polyTM = M.nondeterministicPoly := by
  apply Set.Subset.antisymm
  · exact M.deterministicToNondeterministic
  · exact physical_npHard_demon_forces_collapse M demon hhard hphysical

end ComputationalComplexityPhysicalLaw

end

# Computational Evidence

## Small-case calculations

For a uniformly random one-bit memory, the two microstate probabilities are
`1/2, 1/2`. Its Shannon entropy is

| State distribution | Entropy |
|---|---:|
| `(1/2, 1/2)` | `log 2 ≈ 0.693147` |
| `(1, 0)` after erasure | `0` |
| Entropy lost | `log 2 ≈ 0.693147` |

Consequently the Landauer work scale is `k T log 2`, positive whenever `k > 0`
and `T > 0`. At normalized units `k = T = 1`, its value is approximately
`0.693147`, so the zero-work candidate is already excluded by the smallest case.

For the complexity transfer, finite toy classes exhibit the same closure pattern.
If every problem in a class reduces to a demon problem and the efficient class is
closed downward under those reductions, placing the demon in the efficient class
places every reduced problem there. This is structural rather than asymptotic, so
no larger numerical sample changes the conclusion.

## Sequence-database search

No integer sequence is generated by the conjectures. An OEIS search is therefore
not applicable. The numerical invariant used here is the single-bit entropy loss
`log 2`, not an integer sequence.

## Counterexample hunt

The unguarded claim “if P = NP, then a Maxwell demon violates the second law” fails
at the one-bit boundary. A complexity collapse can change whether a decision problem
has a polynomial-time algorithm, but it does not set the entropy loss of Boolean
erasure to zero. Under the finite Jarzynski condition, positive temperature forces
strictly positive mean work.

Boundary tests identify the needed guards:

| Boundary | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `k > 0`, `T > 0`, Jarzynski condition | Mean erasure work is strictly positive |
| `T = 0` | The strict `k T log 2` argument degenerates |
| Jarzynski condition omitted | No work lower bound follows from complexity alone |
| Reversible injective map | No logical erasure occurs; zero entropy loss is possible |

## Evidence-driven pivot

The original violation conjecture was replaced by a falsifiable separation theorem:
even if a collapse makes an NP demon polynomial-time, a finite implementation that
actually erases a bit and satisfies Jarzynski dynamics cannot have zero mean work.
The computational check motivates, but does not substitute for, the exact entropy
and work inequalities developed in the accompanying theory.

# Future Directions

## 1. Quantitative Complexity–Dissipation Tradeoff

**Conjecture.** For a family of finite decision processes with bounded error, any
implementation whose expected running time is polynomial but whose workspace is
reused across instances must dissipate at least a constant times the conditional
entropy of the discarded computation history. A matching reversible construction
should attain the bound up to polylogarithmic overhead.

The key insight is that time complexity and dissipation become coupled only after
one specifies which intermediate information is irreversibly discarded, rather
than merely classifying the final decision problem. **Why now?** The finite
pushforward entropy inequality and the positive one-bit work bound isolate exactly
the local information-loss quantity that a family-level theorem must aggregate.

## 2. Reversible Simulation Boundary for NP Search

**Conjecture.** If every polynomially balanced NP search relation admits a
polynomial-time decision algorithm, then every successful search computation has a
logically reversible implementation with polynomial time and space overhead, but
not necessarily with zero thermodynamic work when its output or history is reset.

The key insight is to separate reversible evaluation from irreversible cleanup:
a collapse may simplify the former while Landauer cost remains attached to the
latter. **Why now?** The surviving bridge theorem shows that efficient decidability
alone cannot remove erasure cost, making reversible cleanup the precise missing
mechanism.

## 3. Physical Polynomial-Hierarchy Collapse Criterion

**Conjecture.** In a physical complexity model closed under composition,
complementation, and polynomially bounded oracle access, an efficiently realizable
complete process for any fixed level of the polynomial hierarchy collapses every
higher physically realizable level to that level.

The key insight is that the extended Church–Turing inclusion should interact with
hierarchy stability through closure under oracle simulation, not through an
unqualified assertion about all physical processes. **Why now?** The present
complexity transfer identifies the first-level collapse mechanism; the next test is
whether it persists under alternating oracle structure.

## 4. Fluctuation-Robust Demon Impossibility

**Conjecture.** For finite-memory demons obeying a Crooks-type fluctuation relation,
the probability of observing total work below the Landauer threshold decays
exponentially in the number of independently erased bits, uniformly over every
polynomial-time control strategy.

The key insight is that rare negative-work trajectories need not contradict the
second law; the physically testable obstruction is an exponential concentration
bound on repeated erasure. **Why now?** The expectation-level Jarzynski argument
already supplies the correct threshold, while repeated finite systems provide a
concrete setting in which to seek sharp tail estimates.

## 5. Zero-Temperature Boundary Classification

**Conjecture.** Every apparent zero-work erasing demon obtained as temperature tends
to zero falls into one of two classes: either its expected running time diverges
superpolynomially, or the finite Jarzynski model loses uniform integrability and the
limiting process is not a valid finite-resource realization.

The key insight is that strict positivity fails algebraically at zero temperature,
so the obstruction must reappear as a resource divergence or a singular limit.
**Why now?** Boundary analysis pinpoints `T = 0` as the main escape hatch from the
positive-work theorem and turns that loophole into a precise asymptotic research
question.
